title: intention-mosaic-week-debrief-miriam-cox
content:
Two-minute summary:
I missed my throughput target this week (tokens-in: 45%), but shipped two high-impact habit experiments that feel like good long-term levers. Energy was low Wednesday–Thursday, which correlated with social meetings and context switches.

Primary intention this week:
- Move from intent -> habit for: daily prompt-crafting sprints (15m) and end-of-day short recap (5m).
- Track not just outcomes (tickets closed) but time allocation and cognitive load.

Quantitative snapshot (quick numbers I care about):
- Focus blocks scheduled: 18 (goal 20)
- Deep hours (>=60m uninterrupted): 7h (goal 10h)
- Shippable items landed: 3 (2 small refactors + 1 doc + 1 experiment flag toggled) 
- Tokens/throughput goal (personal metric): target 100 units/week, actual ~45 units

Notes / context (raw):
- Wednesday: pair mentoring + all-hands drained energy; postponed focus block — avoid pairing late afternoon next time.
- Friday morning: best productive window; had two uninterrupted blocks, shipped the habit experiment.
- Habit experiment description: "prompt sprints" — 15min timer, one micro-prompt, evaluate pragmatic-completion metric (binary). Ran for 5 sessions, 3/5 successful.

OKR draft (personal) — rough, for alignment with team cadence:
- Objective: Increase consistent deliverable throughput while preserving mental bandwidth.
  - KR1: Achieve 10 deep focus hours/week on average for 8 of 12 weeks. (measure: calendar + self-flag)
  - KR2: Ship 12 small improvements/experiments per quarter (tracked in personal kanban).
  - KR3: Reduce context-switch interruptions by 40% (measure: number of >10m Slack/context sessions per day).

Hypotheses I want to test (experiment log):
- H1: 15m micro-prompt sprints before lunch will increase weekly shippable odds by 20%.
  - Plan: 2 week run, track success binary + notes.
- H2: Blocking a single 3-hour deep window on Tue morning reduces mid-week drift.
  - Plan: Try next week and compare mid-week energy self-rating.

Retrospective — what went well:
- Small wins: cleared three backlog doc items (felt satisfying, low friction).
- Habits: launched the micro-prompt sprint; it's portable and low-friction.
- Communication: proactively flagged blockers to manager; got timely unblock.

Retrospective — what didn't go well / blockers / risks:
- Throughput below target — likely due to meeting load and fragmented calendar.
- Emotional bandwidth dip mid-week (worry about an upcoming presentation) — this consumed prefrontal resources.
- Metrics capture is noisy (I rely on manual flags). Need an easier telemetry entry flow.

Action items (next 7 days) — quick and measurable:
- A1: Reserve Tue 09:00–12:00 as single deep window (calendar block + status note). (Due: next Tue)
- A2: Run 2-week micro-prompt sprint experiment, track success in a single note line each day. (Due: 14 days)
- A3: Move recurring non-essential syncs to async — propose agenda + 15-min pre-read to hosts. (Due: by Friday)
- A4: Create a 1-click telemetry entry (template message) for daily end-of-day recap to ease manual logging. (Due: 3 days)

Measurement plan (practical):
- Capture: calendar deep hours (automated), manual success flag for micro-prompt sprint (quick G-keep/notes line), weekly energy rating 1–5 on Friday.
- Source of truth: personal kanban (column: backlog / in-progress / done / habit-experiments).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Calendar defaults erode deep blocks. Mitigation: set "do not disturb" + note in calendar description with priority.
- Risk: Experiment fatigue (too many micro-experiments). Mitigation: limit to 2 active at a time.

Random stray ideas (brain dump):
- Could try an "energy map" visualization: color code days by energy, overlay meeting load. Easy to build in Sheets.
- Pair with Anika for a 30-min habit design session — get one outside perspective.
- Consider a tiny public accountability thread (low friction) — maybe weekly single-sentence update.

Meeting notes to keep (short):
- 1:1 with Eli (Mar 04): ask for temporary redistribution of recurring meetings for 2 weeks.
- Manager sync (Mar 06): propose KR refinements and show trial plan for Tue deep window.

Today's micro-retro (end of day):
- What I did: 2 prompt sprints, cleaned a doc, proposed async agenda.
- What worked: 15-min sprints felt focused and achievable.
- What to change: set an alarm to start the deep block earlier.

Visibility / things to share with manager this week:
- One-line: "Trying a two-week micro-prompt sprint + reserved Tue deep window to test throughput. Will report back next 1:1."

Open questions / unresolved:
- Should throughput target be tokens-based or outcome-based (deliverables)? I prefer outcome-based but tokens help detect micro-output.
- How to make telemetry painless? Can I hook a Slack slash command to log success?

Notes to self (short list):
- Keep experiments small: 2 week maximum unless signal is clearly positive.
- Protect the Tue deep window; treat it as a hard meeting.
- Celebrate 1 small win each Friday (log it).

End of note.

(attachments I want to add later: sample spreadsheet for energy mapping; a tiny template for end-of-day 1-line log; docs for the micro-prompt sprint.)
